summary: The main article describes an N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) and photocatalyst co-catalyzed decarboxylative radical coupling of carboxylic acids and acyl imidazoles to form ketones. It includes optimization tables, substrate scope figures for two- and three-component couplings, and mechanistic studies including radical clock and Stern-Volmer quenching experiments.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Synthesis of ketones from carboxylic acid derivatives. a Conventional and metal-catalyzed methods for ketone synthesis. TM = transition metal. LA = Lewis Acid. b Earlier ketone synthesis involving NHC-catalyzed radical process. c Two-component coupling using prefunctionalized radical precursors via NHC/photo catalysis. d CF3 radical initiated three-component coupling. e This work: Two/three-component radical coupling for ketone synthesis using carboxylic acids as radical precursors. PC = photo catalyst.
items.description: This figure provides a conceptual overview comparing traditional ketone synthesis methods with the newly developed NHC/photocatalyst dual catalytic approach using carboxylic acids.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction conditions.
items.description: This table details the screening of NHC catalysts, photocatalysts, and reaction components to optimize the yield of the ketone product 3a.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Development of one-pot operation. a One-pot procedure for coupling of two carboxylic acids. b Comparision between one-pot operation and standard conditions.
items.description: This figure illustrates the one-pot protocol for synthesizing ketones directly from two different carboxylic acids using CDI as an activating agent.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Scope of the reaction. Reaction conditions: 1 (1.5 equiv), 2 (0.1 -0.2 mmol), B (20 mol %), PC-3 (1 mol %) and Cs2CO3 (2.0 equiv) in MeCN (2.0 mL), blue LED (Kessil PR160 series, λ max = 427 nm), Ar atmosphere, 30 -40°C, 24 h.
items.description: This figure displays the substrate scope for the two-component coupling, showing various aryl and alkyl ketones synthesized from acyl imidazoles and carboxylic acids.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: Examples of three-component radical relay reactions. Reaction conditions: 1 (2.0 equiv), 2 (0.1 -0.3 mmol, 1.0 equiv), 4 (3.0 equiv), B (20 mol%), PC-3 (1 mol %) and Cs2CO3 (2.0 equiv) in MeCN, blue LED (Kessil PR160 series, λ max = 427 nm), Ar atmosphere, 30 -40°C, 24 h.
items.description: This figure demonstrates the three-component radical relay coupling involving an alkene as the third partner to form complex γ-substituted ketones.

items.heading: Fig. 5
items.caption: Application of the method in modification of drug molecules. Reaction conditions: 1 (1.5 equiv), 2 (0.05-0.1 mmol, 1.0 equiv), B (20 mol%), PC-3 (1 mol %) and Cs2CO3 (2.0 equiv) in MeCN, blue LED (Kessil PR160 series, λ max = 427 nm), Ar atmosphere, 30 -40°C, 24 h.
items.description: This figure showcases the late-stage functionalization of marketed drugs and the coupling of different drug fragments to create new ketone entities.

items.heading: Fig. 6
items.caption: Mechanistic studies. a Reaction in the presence of TEMPO. b Radical clock reaction. c UV -Vis absorption spectra of Int. II and PC-3 . d Stern -Volmer quenching experiments between PC-3 and sodium carboxylate 8 . e Stern -Volmer quenching experiments between Int. II and sodium carboxylate 8 (black line).
items.description: This figure presents experimental evidence for the radical pathway, including TEMPO trapping, radical clock results, and photophysical quenching data.

items.heading: Fig. 7
items.caption: Proposed catalytic cycle. NHC and photocatalyst co-catalyzed mechanism.
items.description: This scheme outlines the proposed dual catalytic cycle involving the formation of acyl azolium intermediates and radical generation via oxidative decarboxylation.
